concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish an algebraic identity, true for all values of its variables, from an equation.
Interpret (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² using a square of side (a + b) partitioned into squares and rectangles.
Use (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² to expand binomials and evaluate squares of numbers.
Factorise perfect-square trinomials, taking out a common factor first where needed.
Use (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² to factorise expressions and compute squares.
Use identities to prove patterns among squares of consecutive numbers.

topics.title: More identities: (a + b + c)² and a² − b²

concepts.learning_objective: Expand and apply (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca.
Apply a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), and Shridharacharya's form a² = (a + b)(a − b) + b², to quick calculations.

topics.title: Factorisation with algebra tiles and by splitting the middle term

concepts.learning_objective: Represent products and factors of quadratic expressions with algebra tiles.
State and use (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab.
Factorise quadratic expressions by splitting the middle term using a + b and ab.
Use (a + b)³ and (a − b)³ to expand and to recognise perfect cubes.
Apply x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²) and x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² − xy + y²).
Use x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − xz − yz) to evaluate expressions.
Simplify rational algebraic expressions by factorising and cancelling non-zero common factors.
Form and factorise quadratic expressions to solve area problems.
